question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{2{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

$$

First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{2{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {coth}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now we need to find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Then, we use the above identity to write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {coth}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{csch}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-1}-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{5}{3}-\frac{5}{4}) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}\end{aligned}
$$
